parsed.process: id retting: separating bast fibre by microbial/chemical degradation of pectin binding the fibres
parsed.current_inefficiency: Retting endpoint is judged by feel/experience, so under-retting leaves fibres bound while over-retting weakens and dirties them, with quality and timing varying widely by method and conditions
parsed.ai_technique: Near-infrared/short-wave-infrared hyperspectral imaging coupled with a gradient-boosted regression model (XGBoost) calibrated against pectin-content/fibre-strength reference assays
parsed.how_it_improves: Inputs: line-scan NIR-SWIR hyperspectral cubes (~900-1700 nm) of retting straw sampled periodically (or in-line on a conveyor), where pectin, cellulose and lignin have characteristic absorption features. Model: an XGBoost regressor trained on spectra labelled with lab-measured residual pectin (uronic-acid assay) and tensile fibre strength, outputting a continuous 'retting degree' index per sample. Actionable output: a calibrated endpoint alarm that flags the optimal harvest window (pectin sufficiently degraded, cellulose not yet attacked) and a spatial map of uneven retting across a field/pond batch. Efficiency gain: replaces subjective feel-testing with an objective, repeatable pectin-state readout, cutting both under- and over-retting losses, tightening fibre-strength variance, and standardising timing across pond/stream/field methods.
parsed.why_not_done_before: Hyperspectral+ML is mature for grain and forage quality but retting is a low-tech, smallholder/heritage process with no instrumentation budget and no public spectral library labelled against pectin-degradation reference assays; building that calibration set (destructive uronic-acid + tensile testing across retting stages) is the unglamorous bottleneck nobody has funded for flax/hemp retting specifically
parsed.primary_quote: Retting endpoint is judged by feel/experience

reasoning_trace.reasoning: The inefficiency is fundamentally a hidden-state estimation problem: the operator cannot directly see residual pectin, the very compound whose degradation defines the endpoint. NIR-SWIR hyperspectral imaging directly senses the molecular bonds of pectin/cellulose, and gradient-boosted regression is a well-proven, sample-efficient way to map noisy spectra to a continuous chemical target without huge deep-learning datasets. This is concretely buildable: spectrometers, XGBoost, and uronic-acid assays all exist today; an engineer needs only to collect labelled retting-stage spectra. I rejected a YOLO/CNN visual classifier because surface colour/texture (what 'feel and experience' already approximate) is a weak, confounded proxy for internal pectin state, whereas SWIR sees the chemistry directly.
reasoning_trace.decision: Use NIR-SWIR hyperspectral imaging + XGBoost regression calibrated to residual pectin and fibre strength to give an objective retting-endpoint index
reasoning_trace.confidence: high - the sensing physics and the ML method are both established; the only real work is assembling the labelled calibration set
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: field moisture, soil/microbial contamination, or straw geometry dominate the SWIR signal enough that pectin features can't be reliably isolated, or if a proprietary industrial flax processor has already deployed exactly this calibration and not published it
